reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) directly supports each premise with specific data on Mn dissolution thermodynamics, diffusion, redox buffering, and observed behavior in 316H stainless steel, though the evidence comes from a single HEA/316H study and does not address Q235 steel or its specific Mn content.
premises: Mn preferentially dissolves in molten fluoride salt over Cr due to lower Gibbs free energy of MnF2 formation
Mn dissolution establishes a Mn/MnF2 redox buffer that thermodynamically suppresses Cr dissolution
Mn has a higher diffusion coefficient than Cr, enabling its sacrificial dissolution
Even low Mn content (~2 wt%) in 316H stainless steel leads to measurable Mn dissolution in salt
The sacrificial Mn mechanism can protect structural alloy constituents from molten salt corrosion
